Who I Am

I grew up asking questions nobody wanted to answer — so I learned to find them myself. Somewhere between numbers and narratives, between a policy brief and a half-read novel, between what is and what ought to be — that is where I live.

I am drawn to systems: how they break, who they leave behind, and the quiet architecture of how they might be repaired. I believe the most dangerous thing a person can carry is an incurious mind — and so I carry instead a notebook, a question, and the stubborn conviction that rigour and empathy are not opposites.

My long game is simple and complicated all at once — to return. To the place I come from, to the people who shaped me, with something useful in my hands.
